entry.title: How Are You Configuring Remote Workers in Employee Central?
entry.content:
Hello SuccessFactors Community,

We’re reviewing how to represent fully remote employees in Employee Central and would appreciate hearing what other organizations are doing.

The standard Location foundation object represents a company’s physical work locations. It doesn’t, by itself, represent a remote employee’s actual work address when that address differs from their assigned office.

Our current approach is to use Work Address Override (WAO) to capture the address where a remote employee performs their work, alongside a work classification field identifying the employee as remote, onsite, or hybrid.

We see some operational considerations with this approach. Downstream integrations and processes need to read from the correct address source for payroll, tax, compliance forms, and reporting. Address changes when an employee moves also need careful handling to keep related records and processes aligned.

What approach does your organization use for remote-worker configuration in Employee Central? Are you satisfied with how it supports ongoing monitoring, address changes, and downstream integrations? What would you recommend or do differently?

Thanks for sharing your experience.

entry.title: SAP SuccessFactors OData API: "Entity not deletable" when trying to delete PerEmail record via CPI
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

I'm currently working on an integration scenario in SAP Cloud Integration (CPI) to automate a specific HR process. The goal is to clear/remove the business email address (PerEmail) for active employees who have lost their corporate email account for various reasons, but are still employed in the company.

I've set up a simple integration flow, but when I try to execute the delete operation via the SuccessFactors OData API, the SF API Audit Log returns the following error:

"Entity not deletable"

However, when I log into the SuccessFactors UI and go to the employee's profile, I am able to manually delete the email address without any issues.

Does anyone have an idea why this happens via the OData API and how to bypass or properly handle this restriction? Is there a specific permission, a business rule, or an alternative approach (like upserting with a blank/null value or using composite API) that I should use instead?

Thanks in advance for your help and insights!

entry.title: Time Off – Accrual Recalculation After a Backdated Job Information Change
entry.content:
Scenario:

A customer calculates annual leave entitlement based on employee grade.

Employees in Grade A receive 30 days annually, while Grade B employees receive 24 days.

An employee was promoted from Grade B to Grade A effective July 1, but HR entered the promotion in Employee Central on October 15 with a backdated effective date.

The accrual rule is configured correctly and works for normal grade changes. However, the employee's Time Account still reflects the previous entitlement after the backdated promotion.

Question:

What is the recommended way to trigger Time Off accrual recalculation for a backdated Job Information change when the accrual rule depends on employee grade?

Can the recalculation be triggered automatically through a rule, or does it require a specific recalculation configuration or administrative process?

entry.title: Employee Central - Dynamic Role Approval After a Backdated Business Unit Transfer
entry.content:
Scenario:

A customer uses Dynamic Roles to determine workflow approvers based on Business Unit.

An employee belongs to Business Unit A and submits a workflow on October 10. The workflow is routed to the Business Unit A Head and remains pending.

On October 15, HR enters a backdated Business Unit transfer effective October 1, moving the employee to Business Unit B.

The customer expects the pending workflow to be automatically redirected to the Business Unit B Head because the employee's Business Unit has changed.

Question:

Does SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central automatically re-evaluate Dynamic Role approvers when an employee's Business Unit changes after a workflow has already been initiated?

If the workflow remains assigned to the original approver, what is the recommended approach to handle such scenarios without compromising workflow history and audit requirements?

entry.title: Time Off - Leave Balance Migration During a Mid-Year Implementation
entry.content:
Scenario:

A customer is migrating from a legacy HR system to SAP SuccessFactors in October.

Employees have different annual leave balances, including:

  • Current-year entitlement.

  • Leave already consumed.

  • Carry-forward balances from previous years.

  • Expired carry-forward balances.

  • Approved future leave requests.

The customer wants to migrate the balances without losing historical information or deducting approved future leave twice.

Question:

What is the recommended migration strategy for Time Off balances when implementing SAP SuccessFactors in the middle of a leave year?

Should the project migrate only the available balance, or should separate time accounts be created for current entitlement, carry-forward, and historical adjustments?

How should future-approved absences be handled to avoid duplicate deductions?
